title: Fix Three.js WebGL context loss with React StrictMode
description:
## Problem
React StrictMode double-renders components in development, causing WebGL context loss with Three.js/R3F.

## Root Cause
StrictMode mounts → unmounts → remounts to test cleanup. The R3F Canvas creates a WebGL context on mount, but the context gets lost during the unmount/remount cycle.

## Current versions
- @react-three/fiber: ^9.1.2
- @react-three/drei: ^10.0.6
- React: 19.x

## Evidence
- Works in production (no StrictMode effects)
- Works locally without StrictMode
- Fails locally with StrictMode enabled
notes: Fixed by disabling StrictMode in dev mode. Root cause: R3F WebGL context doesn't survive StrictMode's mount/unmount/remount cycle in React 19.

~130 lines with manual spring physics and clip sampling

## New File Contents (Complete Replacement)
```typescript
import { easings } from '@react-spring/three';
import type * as THREE from 'three';
import { useModelStore } from '../stores/model-store';
import { useModelAnimation } from './useModelAnimation';

interface UseBogieAnimationOptions {
  actions: Record<string, THREE.AnimationAction | null>;
  groupRef: React.RefObject<THREE.Group | null>;
}

/**
 * Hook that handles bogie (rocker) animation with easeOutBounce easing.
 * Animates the robot's suspension based on bogieTarget store value (0-1).
 *
 * Uses the generalized useModelAnimation hook internally.
 */
export function useBogieAnimation({
  actions,
  groupRef,
}: UseBogieAnimationOptions): void {
  useModelAnimation({
    actions,
    groupRef,
    clipName: 'rocker',
    getProgress: () => useModelStore.getState().bogieTarget,
    config: {
      duration: 1500,
      easing: easings.easeOutBounce,
    },
  });
}
```

- Local `sampleTrackAtTime` function (now in animation-utils.ts)
- Manual spring physics (`useSpringValue`, refs)
- Manual clip initialization useEffect

title: Animation not playing after Zustand migration - investigate and fix
description: Animation doesn't play at all after Zustand migration. Any state change (not just lid) can reset/break bogie animation. Root cause: Re-renders from Zustand selector changes may cause useAnimations to return new actions object, invalidating the initialized animation.

title: Investigate: Lid useEffect runs on mount with lidOpen=false
description: In current code, useEffect at line 134-141 reacts to [lidOpen, actions]. On first render, lidOpen=false triggers action.play() backward. In working code, lid animation was only triggered by user clicks (callback), NOT by useEffect. This might mess up animation mixer state.

title: Investigate: useEffect ordering - lid reaction vs lid init
description: Lid reaction useEffect (line 134) runs BEFORE lid init useEffect (line 197). Reaction sets paused=false and play(), then init sets time=0 and paused=true. This ordering might cause animation mixer issues.

title: Key difference: Working code triggers lid via callback, current via useEffect
description: WORKING (commit 830709): internalSetLidOpen() callback triggers animation only on user click. CURRENT: useEffect([lidOpen, actions]) triggers on mount AND on lidOpen changes. Solution: Skip animation on first render OR use callback pattern like working code.

title: Approach 1: Add hasMounted ref to skip lid animation on first render
description: Add const hasMountedRef = useRef(false). In lid useEffect, check if (!hasMountedRef.current) { hasMountedRef.current = true; return; }. This prevents the lid animation from playing on first render.

title: Approach 2: Use previous lidOpen value to detect actual changes
description: Add const prevLidOpenRef = useRef(lidOpen). In lid useEffect, check if (prevLidOpenRef.current === lidOpen) return; else prevLidOpenRef.current = lidOpen. This only animates when lidOpen actually changes, not on mount.

title: Verify fix: Both bogie and lid animations work correctly
description: Test: 1. Click wheels - bogie animates. 2. Drag Leva bogie slider - animates. 3. Click lid - opens/closes. 4. Change bogie to 0.0, toggle lid - bogie stays at 0.0 (not reset to 0.5)

title: Investigate: useAnimations returns new actions object on re-render
description: When E-model re-renders (from any Zustand state change), useAnimations might return a NEW actions object. The rockerInitializedRef guards the old action, but useFrame now references a NEW actions.rocker that was never initialized. Need to verify if actions reference is stable across re-renders.

title: Approach 3: Store initialized action in ref, re-init only when actions.rocker changes
description: Use rockerActionRef = useRef(null). In useEffect, check if actions.rocker !== rockerActionRef.current, then initialize and store. In useFrame, use rockerActionRef.current instead of actions.rocker. This handles actions object instability.

title: Rename prevRockerActionRef to rockerActionRef (repurpose debug ref)
description: The debug ref prevRockerActionRef already stores the initialized action. Rename it to rockerActionRef for clarity since it will be the source of truth for useFrame.

title: Update useFrame to use rockerActionRef.current instead of actions.rocker
description: In useFrame, change: const rockerAction = actions.rocker; to: const rockerAction = rockerActionRef.current; This ensures useFrame always uses the initialized action, not a new unstable reference.

title: Update init useEffect: re-init when actions.rocker identity changes
description: Modify the guard logic: instead of just checking rockerInitializedRef, also check if actions.rocker !== rockerActionRef.current. If identity changed, re-initialize and update the ref. This handles hot-reload and edge cases.

title: Approach 4: Subscribe to Zustand outside React, use callbacks like working code
description: Instead of using useEffect to react to state changes, use useModelStore.subscribe() to watch for changes and trigger animations via callbacks (like working code). This avoids re-render issues entirely. Subscribe in useEffect with empty deps, unsubscribe on unmount.
